- Vectors $p, r, x$ of size $n$ (dimension of the solution space).
- Scalar variables for step sizes and norms.
Compute initial residual $r_0 = b - A x_0 = b$.
Set initial search direction $p_0 = A^T r_0$.
Compute matrix-vector product $q = A p_k$.
Update solution: $x_{k+1} = x_k + \alpha_k p_k$.
Update residual: $r_{k+1} = r_k - \alpha_k q$.
The preconditioned residual is $\tilde{r}_{k+1} = M^{-1} r_{k+1}$.
Compute new search direction: $p_{k+1} = A^T \tilde{r}_{k+1} + \beta_k p_k$.

Compute $\rho_{k+1} = \tilde{r}_{k+1}^T r_{k+1}$ (or $r_{k+1}^T r_{k+1}$ depending on specific CGLS variant, but standard CGLS uses $r^T r$ for $\rho$ and preconditioning affects the direction update).
*Note: Standard CGLS does not use preconditioning in the $\rho$ calculation, but applies it to the residual before computing the next $p$.
The exact formula for $\beta_k$ is $\beta_k = \rho_{k+1} / \rho_k$.*
Check convergence: if $\|r_{k+1}\|$ is sufficiently small, stop.
